extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent owners, third‑party requesters, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements for (1) inter partes reexamination proceedings (responses, appeals, mergers, certificates, suspension) and (2) filing and processing international design applications under the Hague Agreement through the USPTO (contents, form, fees, transmittal, representation, relief).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely and appropriate response in inter partes reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner fails to file a timely and appropriate response in an inter partes reexamination proceeding, the prosecution in the reexamination proceeding will be a terminated prosecution and the Director will proceed to issue and publish a certificate concluding the reexamination proceeding under § 1.997 in accordance with the last action of the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims are found patentable and the patent owner fails to file a timely and appropriate response to any Office action, further prosecution is limited to the claims found patentable at the time of the failure and to any claims added thereafter which do not expand the scope of those claims. If the action by the patent owner is a bona fide attempt and substantially complete but omits some matter inadvertently, an opportunity to explain and supply the omission may be given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to revive terminated or limited reexamination prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: If a response by the patent owner is not timely filed, a petition may be filed pursuant to § 1.137 to revive a reexamination prosecution terminated under § 1.957(b) or limited under § 1.957(c) if the delay in response was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition to revive is available only where the delay was unintentional and must follow § 1.137 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board under 35 U.S.C. 134(c) are conducted according to part 41 of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the PTAB rules in part 41 for appeal briefing, procedures, and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return of jurisdiction from PTAB and termination of appeal proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Jurisdiction over an inter partes reexamination proceeding passes to the examiner after a decision by the PTAB upon transmittal of the file to the examiner; upon judgment in the appeal before the PTAB, if no further appeal has been taken, the prosecution will be terminated and the Director will issue and publish a certificate under § 1.997 concluding the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit has been filed, that appeal is considered terminated when the mandate is issued by the Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening after final PTAB decision
rubrics_metrics.description: When a PTAB decision on appeal has become final for judicial review, prosecution of an inter partes reexamination proceeding will not be reopened or reconsidered by the primary examiner except under the provisions of § 41.77 and only with the written authority of the Director, and then only for the consideration of matters not already adjudicated, sufficient cause being shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reopening is exceptional — requires Director's written authority and sufficient cause, and is limited to matters not adjudicated by the PTAB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit — eligibility and steps
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner or third party requester who is a party to a PTAB appeal and dissatisfied with the PTAB decision may, subject to § 41.81, appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit and be a party to any appeal thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps include: (1) timely file a written notice of appeal directed to the Director in accordance with §§ 1.302 and 1.304 at the USPTO; (2) file a copy of the notice of appeal and pay the fee in the Federal Circuit according to its rules; (3) serve a copy of the notice on every other party per § 1.248. Cross-appeals and participation rules are also specified (see next entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation and cross-appeal procedures in Federal Circuit appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: A party electing to participate in an appellant’s appeal must, within fourteen days of service of the appellant’s notice of appeal or notice of cross appeal, file a written notice directed to the Director electing to participate and follow corresponding filing and service requirements in the Federal Circuit and with other parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File notice to Director (by mail/hand to General Counsel per § 104.2), file copy in the Federal Circuit per its rules, and serve all other parties per § 1.248. Note historical limitation: for reexaminations commenced prior to Nov. 2, 2002 the third party requester is precluded from appealing or participating in appeals to the Federal Circuit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preclusion of third party requester appeals for early proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding any provision of the rules, in any reexamination proceeding commenced prior to November 2, 2002, the third party requester is precluded from appealing and cross appealing any PTAB decision to the Federal Circuit, and is precluded from participating in any appeal taken by the patent owner to the Federal Circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a temporal exception affecting rights to appeal for early-filed proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of prior or concurrent proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In any inter partes reexamination proceeding the patent owner shall call the attention of the Office to any prior or concurrent proceedings in which the patent is or was involved (including interference or PTAB trial, reissue, reexamination, or litigation) and the results of such proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any person may file a paper notifying the Office of a prior or concurrent proceeding, but such paper must be limited to merely providing notice of the other proceeding without discussion of issues of the current reexamination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of inter partes reexamination due to litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent in inter partes reexamination is or becomes involved in litigation, the Director shall determine whether or not to suspend the inter partes reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director has discretion to suspend; separate stricter rule applies where an interference or trial before PTAB is involved (see next entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension when interference or PTAB trial is involved
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent in inter partes reexamination is or becomes involved in an interference or trial before the PTAB, the Director may suspend the inter partes reexamination, interference, or trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director will not consider a request to suspend an interference or trial unless a motion under § 41.121(a)(3) to suspend has been presented to, and denied by, an administrative patent judge and the request is filed within ten (10) days of the judge's denial or within other time set by the judge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merger of concurrent reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If any reexamination is ordered while a prior inter partes reexamination proceeding is pending and prosecution in the prior proceeding has not terminated, the Office may merge the two proceedings or suspend one of them. Where merger is ordered, the merged examination will normally result in issuance and publication of a single reexamination certificate under § 1.997.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an inter partes reexamination (filed under § 1.913) is merged with an ex parte reexamination (filed under § 1.510) the merged proceeding will be governed by §§ 1.902–1.997, except rights of any third party requester of the ex parte are governed by §§ 1.510–1.560.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merger of reissue application and inter partes reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reissue application and an inter partes reexamination proceeding are pending concurrently on a patent, the Office may merge the proceedings or suspend one. Where merger is ordered, the merged proceeding will be conducted in accordance with §§ 1.171–1.179.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner must place and maintain the same claims in the reissue application and the inter partes reexamination during the merged proceeding. Third party requester participation is limited to issues within inter partes scope. Examiner actions and responses apply to both files. Any inter partes reexamination merged with a reissue application shall be concluded by the grant of the reissued patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of third party requester participation rights in merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: When a third party requester is involved in one or more proceedings that are merged, the merger will be accomplished so as to preserve the requester’s right to participate to the extent provided in the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In merged proceedings involving different requesters, any paper filed by one party shall be served on all other parties of the merged proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance and publication of inter partes reexamination certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: To conclude an inter partes reexamination proceeding the Director will issue and publish an inter partes reexamination certificate in accordance with 35 U.S.C. 316 setting forth the results of the proceeding and the content of the patent following the reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate will be sent to the patent owner and a copy to the third party requester. A certificate that cancels all claims means no further Office proceedings will be conducted for that patent. A reissued patent concluding a merged proceeding constitutes the reexamination certificate. Notice of issuance will be published in the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions related to international design applications
rubrics_metrics.description: In subpart I: 'Article' means an article of the Hague Agreement; 'Regulations' means the Common Regulations Under the 1999 and 1960 Acts; 'Rule' means one of the Regulations; 'Administrative Instructions' refers to Rule 34 instructions; '1960 Act' means the Act signed at The Hague Nov. 28, 1960; other terms not defined here are as defined in Article 1, Rule 1, and 35 U.S.C. 381.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the definitional baseline for applying the Hague Agreement provisions in USPTO practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO as an office of indirect filing — functions
rubrics_metrics.description: As an office of indirect filing, the USPTO shall accept international design applications where the applicant’s Contracting Party is the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major functions include: receiving and according a receipt date; collecting and, when required, transmitting fees due; determining compliance with part 5 requirements; and transmitting the international design application to the International Bureau unless national security prescriptions prevent transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO as a designated office — functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will act as a designated office for international design applications in which the United States has been designated as a Contracting Party in which protection is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major functions include: accepting for national examination international design applications that satisfy the Hague Agreement and Regulations; performing examination in accordance with 35 U.S.C. chapter 16; and communicating results of examination to the International Bureau.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Bureau functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau (WIPO) is the coordinating body under the Hague Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions include: receiving international design applications directly or indirectly; collecting required fees and crediting designation fees; reviewing applications for compliance with formal requirements; translating applications for recordation/publication; registering international designs in the International Register; publishing registrations in the International Designs Bulletin; and sending copies of publications to each designated office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file an international design application through the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Only persons who are nationals of the United States or who have a domicile, habitual residence, or a real and effective industrial or commercial establishment in the territory of the United States may file international design applications through the USPTO as an office of indirect filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the USPTO will accept applications from such persons, an international design application designating the United States may be refused by the Office as a designated office if the applicant is not qualified under 35 U.S.C. chapter 11 to be an applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory contents of an international design application
rubrics_metrics.description: An international design application shall be in English, French, or Spanish and shall contain or be accompanied by: (1) a request for international registration; (2) prescribed data concerning the applicant; (3) the prescribed number of copies of a reproduction or specimens of the industrial design (subject to deferment rules); (4) an indication of the product(s) to which the design relates; (5) an indication of the designated Contracting Parties; and (6) the prescribed fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproductions or specimens must be presented in the prescribed manner; for two-dimensional designs with a deferment request, specimens may substitute for reproductions as allowed by the Hague Agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional/optional contents and Contracting Party-specific mandatory elements
rubrics_metrics.description: An international design application may contain two or more industrial designs subject to conditions; a request for deferment of publication or immediate publication; and other elements. Where designation of a Contracting Party requires certain elements, the application must include them (e.g., identity of creator, brief description of reproduction/characteristic features, a claim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other optional items include name/address of representative, priority claim, Paris Convention exhibition declaration, administrative instructions items, statements of material information, and proposed translations. The application must include elements specifically required by designated Contracting Parties under Article 5(2) and relevant Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents when the United States is designated
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the general mandatory requirements, an international design application designating the United States shall contain: (1) a claim; (2) indications concerning the identity of the creator (inventor) in accordance with Rule 11(1); and (3) the inventor’s oath or declaration (§§ 1.63 and 1.64).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements in §§ 1.63(b) and 1.64(b)(4) to identify each inventor by legal name, mailing address, and residence, and identification of the residence/mailing address of person signing a substitute statement, are satisfied by presenting such information in the international design application prior to international registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and signature requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The international design application shall be presented on the official form (Rules 7(1) and 1(vi)) and shall be signed by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the official form and ensure applicant signature to satisfy formal presentation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date of an international design application in the United States
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to paragraph (b), the filing date of an international design application in the United States is the date of international registration determined by the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the applicant believes the application is entitled to a U.S. filing date other than the date of international registration, the applicant may petition the Director (with the prescribed fee and a showing) to accord a different U.S. filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description/specification requirement for U.S. designation
rubrics_metrics.description: An international design application designating the United States must include a specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112 and preferably include a brief description of the reproduction pursuant to Rule 7(5)(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specification should satisfy the U.S. statutory specification requirements and describe the views of the reproductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim wording for U.S. designation
rubrics_metrics.description: The specific wording of the claim in an international design application designating the United States shall be in formal terms to the ornamental design for the article (specifying name of article) as shown, or as shown and described. More than one claim is neither required nor permitted for purposes of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a single formal ornamental-design claim specifying the article name; do not include multiple claims for U.S. purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproductions compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproductions shall comply with the requirements of Rule 9 and Part Four of the Administrative Instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Rule 9 and Administrative Instructions regarding number, format, views, margins, labeling, and quality of reproductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimens allowed with deferment request (and restrictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a request for deferment of publication has been filed for a two‑dimensional industrial design, the international design application may include specimens of the design in accordance with Rule 10 and Part Four of the Administrative Instructions. Specimens are not permitted in applications that designate the United States or any other Contracting Party which does not permit deferment of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specimens are only available for designs with permitted deferment and cannot be used when U.S. designation is included or when a designated party prohibits deferment/specimens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferment of publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The international design application may contain a request for deferment of publication, provided the application does not designate the United States or any other Contracting Party which does not permit deferment of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferment choice interacts with whether the U.S. or other Contracting Parties are designated; selecting deferment may preclude U.S. designation.

rubrics_metrics.name: International design application fees and payment methods
rubrics_metrics.description: International design applications filed through the Office as an office of indirect filing are subject to a transmittal fee (amounts vary by entity status). The schedule of fees and designation fees are set in the Regulations and on the WIPO website. Fees required by the International Bureau may be paid either directly to the IB or through the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmittal fee table: micro entity $26.00, small entity $52.00, other than small or micro entity $130.00 (as provided). IB fees may be paid in Swiss currency directly to IB or through the Office in U.S. dollars; payments through the Office may subject applicants to additional amounts where currency conversion results in IB receiving less than prescribed amounts. Renewal fees to IB are not required to maintain a U.S. patent; designation fee for the U.S. consists of a first part in Swiss currency (per Hague Rule 28) and a second part (issue fee) payable per § 1.18(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation before IB and USPTO for international design applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may appoint a representative before the International Bureau in accordance with Rule 3. Applicants may be represented before the Office as an office of indirect filing by a practitioner registered or granted limited recognition to practice before the Office in patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointment must be in writing signed by the applicant, give the practitioner power to act, and specify the practitioner's name and registration or limited recognition number. An appointment made in the international design application that complies with these requirements will be effective as an appointment before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence address for international design applications filed via the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may specify a correspondence address for correspondence sent by the Office as an office of indirect filing. Where no such address is specified, the Office will use the address of the applicant’s appointed representative or, where no representative is appointed, the address specified in Administrative Instruction 302.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure a correspondence address is specified to control where USPTO sends communications; otherwise representative or default addresses will be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for transmittal of application to the International Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to payment of the transmittal fee, transmittal of the international design application to the International Bureau shall be made by the Office as provided by Rule 13(1). At transmittal, the Office will notify the IB of the date it received the application and will notify the applicant of the Office receipt and transmittal dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No copy may be transmitted to the IB or foreign designated office unless part 5 requirements are satisfied. Once transmittal is effected, except for matters properly before the USPTO as an office of indirect filing or as a designated office, all further correspondence should be sent directly to the IB. The USPTO generally will not forward communications received after transmittal; any reply to an invitation by the IB must be filed directly with the IB to avoid abandonment or loss of rights under Article 8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief from prescribed time limits (unintentional delay) for international design applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant’s delay in failing to act within prescribed time limits under the Hague Agreement was unintentional, a petition may be filed to excuse the failure to act as to the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A grantable petition must be accompanied by: (1) a copy of any invitation from the International Bureau setting the prescribed time limit; (2) the required reply (unless previously filed); (3) the fee set forth in § 1.17(m); and (4) a certified copy of the originally filed international design application (or proof the Office already has a copy) and a translation into English if it was filed in another language.
